To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we provide a theoretical analysis of knowledge graph relation representation, (2) we categorize knowledge graph relations into semantic types, (3) we show that the empirical properties of the relation representations and the performance of the state-of-the-art models are justified by our theoretical analysis, and (4) we provide a set of recommendations for knowledge graph embedding methods.

knowledge graph embeddings can be categorized into three types: (i) symmetric, (ii) asymmetric, and (iii) asymmetric with a single direction of bias, and (iii), the performance of state-of-the-art knowledge graph embedding methods can be explained using our categorization.

1) knowledge graph relations fall into three categories: (1) symmetric, (2) antisymmetric and (3) asymmetric, 2) each category requires different representation, 3) the representation requirements are reflected by the empirical properties of the embeddings, and 4) the empirical properties of embeddings are related to the performance of the models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to interpret knowledge graph relation representations from word embeddings, which has important implications for their use and design.

how knowledge graph relations can be represented by embeddings, how these representations are used in inference and how these relate to word embeddings and the latent structure of the knowledge graph.
how to better understand knowledge graph representation models and their performance, and how this understanding can be used to guide the development of new models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

“The performance of knowledge graph embedding methods is determined by the quality of their relation representations, and that the quality of relation representations is determined by their capacity to capture the underlying latent semantic structure of relations.”
knowledge graph relation embeddings are not random, but they are also not as interpretable as word embeddings.
the relation representations learned by the models are not only interpretable in the sense that they can be explained by the theoretical framework, but that they also have a high practical value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the latent structure of semantic relations can be explained by the properties of their word embedding representations.
the knowledge graph representation learning methods can be categorized into three types according to the way how the relations are represented.
the latent structure of semantic relations in a knowledge graph can be explained by the same properties as word embedding representations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

knowledge graph relation embeddings can be interpreted as a combination of semantic information and a relation-specific transformation, with the latter providing the basis of the model's predictive performance.
knowledge graph relation embeddings should be interpretable and should reflect the underlying semantics of their corresponding relation.
the latent space of knowledge graph representation models is not a uniform space, but rather is partitioned into three sub-spaces, each of which captures a specific type of relation.
